data.problem: Provide reliable staged and unstaged git changes for the active folder/project, including file tree and hunk/line metadata, and feed that data into an existing diff-capable review UI.
constraints: Must preserve active-directory semantics (`Instance.directory`) while optionally supporting repo-root scope (`Instance.worktree`).
Need explicit staged/unstaged separation (current APIs merge or flatten state).
Should handle large diffs and binary files without blocking UI or returning oversized payloads.
Prefer compatibility with existing unified-diff renderers already in TUI/web share surfaces.

options.name: Add stage-aware git review endpoint (list + lazy diff)
options.approach: Introduce a dedicated server route that returns `staged` and `unstaged` file lists first (status, counts, binary flags), then fetches per-file unified diffs/hunks on demand. Back it with git porcelain + `git diff --cached` and `git diff` executed in `Instance.directory`.
options.what_we_learn: Whether current server/session architecture can support accurate stage separation, how much payload reduction lazy loading gives, and what hunk metadata shape the UI actually needs.
options.risk_if_wrong: Medium: requires new API contract and parser decisions; may expose edge cases (renames, deletions, partially staged files).

options.name: Fast prototype from existing APIs
options.approach: Build a review panel using `/file/status` and `/file/content` only, reusing existing diff rendering components. Use it to validate UX flow quickly, accepting temporary limits (no true staged/unstaged split).
options.what_we_learn: UI information density needs, navigation ergonomics, and whether current `FileContent.patch` granularity is enough for reviewers.
options.risk_if_wrong: High for final goal: cannot faithfully separate staged vs unstaged, and deleted/untracked behavior is incomplete.

options.name: Server-side parse of raw git commands only
options.approach: Keep transport minimal by returning parsed results from `git status --porcelain`, `git diff --cached`, and `git diff` in one call (no session/snapshot coupling), with optional repo-root mode toggle.
options.what_we_learn: How robust a raw-git parser is across rename/binary/submodule cases and whether a single endpoint can cover both CLI and UI consumers.
options.risk_if_wrong: Medium-high: parser complexity and portability concerns; less reuse of existing File/Snapshot abstractions.

data.recommendation: Option 1 first: it is the best learning-speed/accuracy balance because it satisfies staged-vs-unstaged requirements early while keeping risk controlled through list-first lazy hydration and reuse of existing diff viewers.
